messages:
sam: quick question — were designing envelope encryption for the inference path. looking for guidance on DEK caching across services: how long should DEKs live in memory, should we persist wrapped DEKs in redis, and how to avoid hammering KMS during bursts?

marta: good call. TL;DR: hybrid cache + async rewrap. keep hot DEKs in-process short-lived, store wrapped DEKs in a shared encrypted store, and coalesce KMS requests.

jen: agree. constraints: low-latency token generation path hits per-request. we want <20ms p95 for DEK fetch+unwrap. calling KMS on every request is non-starter.

infra-eng: proposal from infra: per-worker in-memory DEK cache with TTL=10m, fallback to redis (wrapped DEK) if miss, and a single-flight rewrap/refresh to avoid thundering herd.

sam: 10m feels short — what about rotation requirements? and rewrap frequency when KEK rotates?

marta: separate concepts: DEK TTL for perf vs KEK rotation policy for security. recommended: DEK TTL 5-15m for hot paths, but keep wrapped DEK blobs persisted in redis/backing store indefinitely with version metadata so we can rewrap on KEK rotation.

security-oncall: audit notes: every KMS Decrypt/Encrypt/GenerateDataKey call must be logged with principal, key_id, operation, request_id, and trace id. forward logs to SIEM and pin retention to compliance policy.

jen: example flow I sketched:
```
# on request
if in_memory_cache.has(key_id): use DEK
else if shared_store.has(wrapped_dek):
    wrapped = shared_store.get(key_id)
    dek = KMS.decrypt(wrapped)  # single KMS call per cold worker startup
    in_memory_cache.set(key_id, dek, ttl=600)
else:
    dek, wrapped = KMS.generate_data_key(key_id)
    shared_store.put(key_id, wrapped, meta=version, last_rewrap_ts)
    in_memory_cache.set(key_id, dek, ttl=600)
```

marta: add singleflight/coalescing around KMS.decrypt and KMS.generate to ensure only one worker makes the KMS call when cache is cold. also jitter retries and backoff.

infra-eng: for redis we store only the KMS-wrapped DEK and metadata: key_id, dek_version, wrapped_by_kek_version, last_rewrap_ts, integrity_hmac. never store plaintext DEKs in redis.

sam: rewrap strategy when rotating KEKs? background job to rewrap all wrapped DEKs with new KEK version and update metadata? what about live revocations?

marta: yes — background rewrap (rehydrate->decrypt with old KEK via KMS.rewrap or decrypt+encrypt depending on cloud) and write new wrapped blob atomically with version. for emergency revocation: mark the KEK as revoked in control plane and deny future KMS.decrypt for that KEK, then trigger forced rewrap or DEK rotation for affected resources.

security-oncall: make sure RBAC: application services have only 'Decrypt' on KEK via an envelope-delegate role, and a separate key-admin role has rewrap/rotate permission. rotate admin creds routinely.

jen: scaling hints: 1) use local in-memory cache per worker to minimize network IO. 2) cache size bounded by active key_id set. 3) use HSM-backed KMS for Rewrap when available (AWS ReEncrypt or GCP rewrap) to avoid plaintext exposure in our infra.

infra-eng: KMS quotas — coalesce and batch generate-data-key ops during scaling events. pre-warm cache when autoscaling up: run a scheduled warmup that reads wrapped DEKs and performs one decrypt per instance before marking ready.

sam: what TTLs for non-hot paths (batch jobs)?

marta: for batch, you can accept longer DEK TTLs (hours) and more tolerant latency, but still don't store plaintext DEKs anywhere persistent. prefer ephemeral in-memory until job completes.

security-oncall: incident playbook snippets: if KMS key compromise suspected: 1) revoke KEK, 2) stop issuing new decrypts, 3) rotate DEKs for sensitive resources asynchronously, 4) notify affected teams, 5) run audit on recent decrypts. keep playbook steps scripted and tested.

sam: any specific numbers for cache TTL and rewrap cadence we can ship as default?

marta: defaults to propose: in-memory DEK TTL = 10m, shared wrapped DEK retention = 90d, KEK rotation = 90d (or per-policy), background rewrap window = 7d after KEK rotation to avoid spikes, singleflight coalesce window = 2s. tweak per workload.

jen: I'll draft infra config and a lightweight library that implements singleflight, cache layers, and audit hooks. will PR with example.

kms-bot: KMS usage tip: consider KMS.GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext where available, and ReEncrypt/Asymmetric rewrap to reduce plaintext exposure in our infra. :gear: 

sam: perfect — thanks everyone. i'll summarize and file a follow-up RFC. :thumbsup:
